abstract: The software package Qcompiler Chen and Wang [2013] provides a general quantum compilation framework, which maps any given unitary operation into a quantum circuit consisting of a sequential set of elementary quantum gates. In this paper, we present an extended software OptQC, which finds permutation matrices $P$ and $Q$ for a given unitary matrix $U$ such that the number of gates in the quantum circuit of $U=Q^{T}P^{T}U^{\prime}PQ$ is significantly reduced, where $U^{\prime}$ is equivalent to $U$ up to a permutation and the quantum circuit implementation of each matrix component is considered separately. We extend further this software package to make use of high-performance computers with a multiprocessor architecture using MPI. We demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the total number of quantum gates required for various unitary operators.

specification.problem: Compile a given unitary U into a quantum circuit of elementary gates with fewer gates by searching for permutation matrices P and Q such that U = Q^T P^T U' P Q, where U' is equivalent to U up to a permutation, and each matrix component is implemented separately (OptQC extending Qcompiler, with MPI parallelization).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the permutation-based gate-count optimization objective only; the search algorithm, decomposition method, and MPI details are not specified in the abstract.

symbols.meaning: Permutation matrices found by the optimizer

equations.label: Permutation factorization
equations.description: Target unitary expressed via permutations P, Q and equivalent unitary U' whose circuit has fewer gates.

equations.label: Gate count minimization
equations.description: Objective: minimize total elementary gate count G over permutations, with each factor compiled separately.
equations.justification: Formalizes the abstract's goal of reducing gate count with components implemented separately; the exact cost function is not given.
assumptions: Total gate count is the sum of per-component counts G(.)

registers.name: q
registers.role: System register on which U is implemented

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary n-qubit input state |psi>; the compiled circuit implements U as a unitary and is not tied to a specific input state.

steps.description: Classically search for permutation matrices P and Q to obtain U' = P Q U Q^T P^T (equivalent to U up to permutation) with lower expected gate cost.
Compile each component (Q, P, U', P^T, Q^T) separately into elementary gates using the Qcompiler-style decomposition.
Concatenate component circuits in order of U=Q^T P^T U' P Q (acting right-to-left: Q, P, U', P^T, Q^T) on register q.

specification.measurement: None intrinsic to the compilation task; the abstract specifies no measurement. For verification, one could measure in the computational basis after applying the compiled circuit to test inputs, which is an assumption.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical optimization only: search over P and Q, compare gate counts of the resulting circuits, and select the minimum. Candidate evaluation is presumably distributed across processors via MPI (details unspecified).
assumptions: Gate-count cost is additive over components.
Register size assumed n qubits with N=2^n; no ancillas.
Circuit applied right-to-left on the same register.
Measurement is not part of the abstract; the computational-basis check is an assumed verification option.
